findings.comment: Employee was observed shutting the faucet with bare hands after washing their hands. Discussed with PIC. The behavior was corrected. Ensure that a barrier is used to shut the facet after handwashing to avoid recontaminating your clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: There was no sani bucket observed in the kitchen as food prep began. Discussed with PIC. Inspector asked PIC to have a Sani bucket made. The Sanitizer for the sani bucket was made and tested at 200 ppm. Ensure that sanitizer is always made and placed in a sani bucket before any food prep or handling at all times.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Inspector was unable to verify the certified food manager’s allergen training certification. PIC told inspector that they had the training done but they cannot find it now however, they will look through their documents and find the certification. Ensure that all paperwork are available and accessible for viewing and verification at all times. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Food handler was observed washing hands without proper technique at the food service area handsink. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier, and a common cloth towel was used to dry hands. Proper technique was discussed and observed in practice upon providing paper towels at the food service area handsink.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Paper towels were not available at the food service area handsink. Paper towels were provided. 
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with Individual, disposable towels or another approved drying option.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114 Sanitizer solutions in food service area sani-bucket and at 3 part sink were at 0ppm chlorine. Solutions were prepared using the wall mounted chemical dispenser at the 3 part sink, and quaternary ammonia based product has been connected for use in the past (see #28 for details). The water is too hot as is to allow for proper concentration, and the dispenser is not intended for use with chlorine product. All chlorine solutions are to be mixed manually. Sani-bucket was remade with fresh solution and observed at 100ppm. 
A chlorine solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration of solutions.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Fry baskets were observed with stuck on food debris. Ensure fry baskets are properly cleaned and sanitized at the end of operations daily.
Hood filters were soiled with grease and dust buildup above the fryer and stove. Clean hood filters as needed to eliminate buildup of dust and grease.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 A pan of potatoes without a date mark was observed in the bottom of the prep cooler in the food service area. Potatoes were a menu item from the weekend prior and were removed for discard. Ensure proper date marks are on all prepared foods, and that foods are used or discarded w/in 7 days.
Ready to eat time/temperature control for safety foods shall be clearly dated after preparation (foods made on-site) or after original packaging is opened (commercially processed foods) and shall be used or discarded within 7 days when held under refrigeration. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1. If products are frozen, then dates need to be changed and documented accordingly to reflect proper time frame for use and ensure the foods are used or discarded within a total of 7 days.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-202.12 A 5 gallon bucket of chlorine sanitizer intended for use with a low temperature chemical sanitizing dish machine was observed in use with the wall mounted chemical dispenser at the 3 part sink. The dispenser at the 3 part sink is intended for use with quat sanitizer not the product provided.  The temperature at the dispenser is too hot for chlorine based products. The chlorine based product was not dispensing at proper concentration. The chemical line was removed from the dish machine sanitizer bucket. Cease the use of 5 gallon buckets of dish machine chemicals with the wall mounted dispenser. Provide proper quat and detergent products for the dispenser or provide another means for preparing sanitizer solutions. 
Poisonous or toxic materials shall be used according to manufacturer's use directions included in labeling.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
3-501.15 Potato salad prepared prior to inspector's arrival was observed with internal temperatures of 46F-48F. Based on information provided the potatoes were boiled, cooled, and mixed with other ingredients within the last 2hrs. Product was still in the process of cooling in the top of the prep cooler and was mounded well above the fill line in the container. Monitoring of time and temperature during cooling and methods to allow for rapid chilling were discussed. A portion of the potato salad was removed and placed in the bottom of the prep cooler for storage.
When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be: (1) Arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls; and (2) Loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. 
Time and temperature need to be monitored during cooling to ensure foods are cooling quickly and properly.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 PIC working at the time of inspection does not currently have a food manager certification. Course work was completed on-line, but PIC has not yet taken the test for certification. Information for testing was provided (see general comments for details).
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 PIC was observed drying his hands with paper towels, turning off the manual faucet, and then continuing to dry his hands with the same paper towels. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. Hands should be thoroughly dried prior to using the paper towels to shut off the faucet. If additional drying of hands is needed, then retrieve a new paper towel to finish drying hands instead of continuing to use the paper towels just used to shut off the faucet. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11 Soufflé cup was observed in an open package of dry parmesan in the reach-in cooler at the food service area. Soufflé cup was removed and discarded. Use proper scoops when dispensing foods. 
Except when washing fruits and vegetables or when ingredients will be added to food that is being fully cooked/has a kill step for pathogens, food employees may not contact exposed, ready-to-eat food with their bare hands and shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing equipment.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12 Paper towel dispenser was empty at the prep kitchen handsink. Paper towels were provided. 
Later paper towels were observed to be absent from the food service area. Paper towels were provided. Ensure soap and paper towels are always available to allow for proper handwashing. 
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with Individual, disposable towels or another approved drying option.
findings.citation_text:
5-501.16 Waste receptacle was on the opposite end of the food service area, and another container was not available for disposal of paper towels after handwashing. A small metal container was provided for disposal of paper towels generated during handwashing.   
If disposable towels are used at handwashing lavatories, a waste receptacle shall be located at each lavatory or group of adjacent lavatories.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Paper boat of seasoning used for flatbread pizza was uncovered by the pizza oven. The seasoning was uncovered overnight and was discarded. Ensure that all seasonings and liquids used in food prep are covered during slow periods and for long-term overnight storage.
Food shall be protected from cross contamination by storing food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings and separating fruits and vegetables, before they are washed from ready to eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114 & 4-702.11 Quat product used as sanitizer was empty. Dishes were done prior to inspector's arrival, and PIC was not certain when the product ran out. A bottle of different quat product was provided for use. When dispensed the concentration was ~300ppm, and the effective range for the product is 150-400ppm. Ensure chemical used for sanitization is always available and at proper concentration. All dishes were to be sanitized prior to use. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.
Utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use after cleaning.

4-602.1 Stems of the digital food thermometers were soiled with food debris, and one of the cases was also observed to be soiled. Cleaning and maintenance of food thermometers were discussed. Thermometers and cases were cleaned during inspection. 
Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage. Clean and sanitize the stems of food thermometers between uses. If sanitizer solution or alcohol wipes are used to wipe stems during prep, then make sure stems are cleaned and sanitized up to every 4 hours after continuous use. Maintain the cases clean. 

Fry baskets were observed with stuck on food debris. PIC noted the fryer is currently not in use and needs to be repaired
 Clean the fry baskets and store them in an area protected from potential contamination until the fryer is available for use again.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.12 Dried food splash was observed inside the microwave in the prep kitchen. Cleaning frequency was discussed.
The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Open package of spinach and pans of chicken were not date marked in the bottom holding area of the prep cooler. One portion of chicken was cooked and cooled the day prior, and the other portion was cooked and cooled the Sunday prior. Date marking was discussed, and products were properly labeled. Ensure all ready to eat, TCS foods that require date marking are dated upon opening/preparation and used or discarded within 7 days. 
Ready to eat time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods shall be clearly dated after preparation (foods made on-site) or after original packaging is opened (commercially processed foods) and shall be used or discarded within 7 days when held under refrigeration. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11 Boxes of bread delivered on Wednesday were observed on the floor in the prep kitchen. Boxes were moved to a storage area off the floor. Ensure proper storage of foods. 
Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food In a clean, dry location; where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and is at least 6 inches above the floor.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 The following nonfood contact surfaces were observed to be soiled: 
A) fryer - general surfaces (grease); and  
B) oven - drip tray (food splash). 
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 The floor in the prep kitchen was soiled with accumulation of food and general debris under equipment and along the floor to wall juncture. Clean the floors throughout daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.
--Hoods baffles were soiled. The baffles over the fryer and oven had grease and dust buildup. Cleaning frequency was discussed.
--Light covers in the hoods were also soiled. Clean the light covers. 
--Electrical outlet cover was loose by the fryer in the food service area. Reattach the cover.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text:
6-303.11 Lights were burnt out in the hoods. Replace the bulbs.
Light intensity shall be at least 50 foot candles (540 lux) at a surface where a food employee is working with food or working with utensils and equipment where employee safety is a factor.

findings.title: Gloves used properly
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Food employee was observed wiping his gloved hands on a wiping cloth in the food service area. Gloves were discarded upon request of inspector. Proper glove use and handwashing were discussed. 
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation. Cease the practice of wiping gloved hands with wiping cloths.
Do not use wiping cloths to wipe hands for any reason.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: 410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07   Certified food managers need to complete online food allergen awareness training. All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 None of the staff working upon arrival of inspector had proof of a food manager certification. Owner and manager of 5Flavors arrived during inspection but did not have copies of manager certifications. Owner of the vineyard arrived later on and would be on-site to oversee operations. 
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager. Proof of manager certifications must be maintained on-site for all CFM.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12 Operator was observed washing hands without proper technique at outside prep kitchen. Manual faucet and paper towel dispenser were touched upon completion of handwashing prior to drying hands. Proper technique was discussed, and operator was advised to lead by example and always wash hands with proper technique regardless of the next task.
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink. Use of forearms and elbows to shut off the manual faucet would also be acceptable.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Food employee working at the food service area was asked how hands were washed prior to putting on gloves since paper towels were not present upon arrival of inspector. Employee noted he washed his hands at the outside prep kitchen prior to coming inside to put on gloves and begin prep. Hands would need to be re-washed upon entering the food service area since door knobs and general surfaces had to be touched prior to entering the food service area before putting on gloves.
Employee was later observed handling a cell phone and did not re-wash hands prior to touching pans of food at the prep cooler. Handwashing was discussed with emphasis on re-washing hands prior to putting on gloves or handling anything related to food after touching cell phones or any surfaces that would potentially contaminate hands.
Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed upon entering the work area, before putting on gloves/between glove changes, and after engaging in activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Paper towels were not present at the food service area handsink. A new roll of paper towels was provided to allow for proper handwashing.
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with Individual, disposable towels or another approved drying option.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Flat containing raw shell eggs was observed on a shelf above ready to eat food in the outdoor prep kitchen cooler. Eggs were removed for use, and proper storage of raw eggs below ready to eat food was discussed.
Food shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display by separating raw animal foods from ready to eat foods.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
3-501.15 Cooked chicken breasts were observed on a baking sheet cooling at room temperature upon arrival of inspector. Chicken had an internal temperature of 73F and was said to have been fully cooked to 165F within the last hour. Chicken was still in the first 2hrs of cooling based on information provided. Staff were advised to cease the practice of cooling at room temperature. Options for rapid chill with ice baths or use of the freezer in the outdoor prep kitchen were discussed. Staff were also advised to monitor the time and temperature during cooling to ensure foods are properly cooled from 135F to 70F within 2hrs and from 70F to 41F/below within an additional 4hrs (total time must not exceed 6hrs). Chicken was placed in the prep cooler to finish cooling.
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13 Portions of homemade, uncooked noodles that were frozen and pulled for service today were thawing at room temperature. Noodles were observed at 60F. Noodle portions were placed in the prep cooler. Staff were advised on proper thawing. 
Time/temperature control for safety food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration at 41°F/below; (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F/below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111 A dozen house flies were observed in the food service area around the floor of the cooking equipment and the prep cooler upon arrival of inspector. A fan was provided to minimize their presence in the food service area. Three to four house flies were also observed in the outside prep kitchen. Pest control was discussed, including proper use of fly strips in approved areas. 
The premises shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence by routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests, using approved methods to control pests, and eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Gloves used properly
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15 Employee left the food service area with gloved hands to retrieve a roll of paper towels. He then entered and exited the building a couple times prior to coming back to the food service area and did not remove gloves prior to returning to prep cooler. Employee was advised on proper glove use and removed gloves to wash hands prior to returning to prep. 
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.13 Facility does not currently have an irreversible registering temperature indicator to verify surface temperature of heat sanitization at the dish machine. Options for measuring the final rinse temperature were discussed. (see general comments for additional information)
In hot water mechanical warewashing operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the utensil surface temperature.
Final rinse temperature of at least 160F must be verified.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment: 410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Proof of food handler certifications were not available for staff that do not have manager certifications. All staff that are not certified food managers need to complete an online food handler certification course that is ANSI and IL approved. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Certified food managers need to complete online food allergen awareness training.
All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Pizza paddle was observed with stuck on food debris. Paddle was cleaned and sanitized during the inspection. 

Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment between uses/up to every 4hrs after continuous use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Carbon and food splash were observed around the burners and on the drip tray of the stove and around the grill. Clean the aforementioned items.

Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.
